physicalNotes: Radius 0.14095816 Jupiter radii from Crossfield et al. 2016 (2016ApJS..226....7C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract): 10,077.4 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.00982 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Kruse et al. 2019 (2019ApJS..244...11K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KRUSE_ET_AL__2019): P 8.05423 d
sources.shape: Crossfield et al. 2016 (2016ApJS..226....7C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CROSSFIELD_ET_AL__2016): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.0708 au and stellar radius 0.675 solar radii; Mayo et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..136M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MAYO_ET_AL__2018): inclination 88.71527 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Kruse et al. 2019 (2019ApJS..244...11K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KRUSE_ET_AL__2019): transit mid-time 2456982.329 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 327 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
